analysis: The method parseTimestampUs splits the input string s by '.' into parts. If s does not contain a dot, parts[1] will cause an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, but this is not a NumberFormatException. Then parts[0] is split by ':' into subparts. Each subparts[i] and parts[1] are parsed with Long.parseLong. The input s is not validated. The split operations may produce empty strings (e.g., consecutive colons or trailing dot) or strings with invalid characters (non-digit, non-sign). Also, the numeric values may exceed the range of long. All these conditions cause Long.parseLong to throw NumberFormatException. There are no checks or validations to avoid these scenarios. Therefore, NumberFormatException is not avoided.
remark: NumberFormatException can be triggered if: (1) any subpart (from splitting by ':') or parts[1] is an empty string (e.g., input like '12::34.56' or '12.34.'), (2) any subpart or parts[1] contains non-numeric characters other than a leading '+' or '-' (e.g., '12a:34:56.78'), (3) the numeric value represented by any subpart or parts[1] is out of the long range (e.g., '99999999999999999999'). The code does not perform any input validation to prevent these.
